Today, March 29, 2025 Governor Maura Healey signed into law bodies to H.62, as amended by S.2506 (which contains the final form of the bill), entitled “An act Relative to Extending Certain Covid-19 Measures Adopted during the State of Emergency” (“ACT). Of interest to all governmental public bodies in Massachusetts, the Act extends until June, 2027, the authority for meetings of multiple-member bodies to be held in an entirely remote or hybrid format. All public bodies may hold fully remote or hybrid meetings, without the physical presence of a quorum of the public body, as long as “adequate, alternative means” of public access is also provided. 

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN IN ACCORDANCE WITH CHAPTER 28 OF THE ACTS OF 2009, SECTIONS 17-20 (FORMERLY SECTION 23B OF CHAPTER 39) OF THE MASSACHUSETTS GENERAL LAWS, THAT A REGULAR MEETING OF THE HOLYOKE SCHOOL COMMITTEE WILL BE HELD ON MARCH 9, 2026.

  1. Updates of Committees 
  • Policy and Governance Subcommittee
    • Order filed by School Committee Member Lubold that in the interest of transparency, public understanding, and engagement, all presentations, slide decks and other major presentation materials included in School Committee Agenda Packets as a pre-read shall, as a matter of standard practice: 1. Include a brief executive summary (no more than one page or one slide) written in plain language that explains: 
  • The presentation’s main purpose
  • The key points or findings
  • Any actions being requested of the committee
  1. Avoid or clearly limit technical jargon, and where specialized or legal terms are necessary, provide a simple definition, “key terms” section in plain language.
  2. Use clear headings and accessible formatting, including inclusive fonts “Arial, Helvetica, Verdana, Calibri, or Open Sans” so that readers with disabilities and diverse language needs can quickly understand what the topic is, why it matters, and what decisions or next steps are being considered.
  3. Ensure materials, to the greatest extent practicable, conform with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended (29 U.S.C. 794d) and align with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 AA, or any successor standard. Order has been complied with. No recommendations 
  • That the School Committee Chair and Superintendent ensure that all communication to the School Committee and public use the full word or term before an acronym can be used.  Rationale: To ensure all parties are clear that they are reading about the same term as acronyms can stand for different terms. Order has been complied with. No recommendations
  • Finance and Operations Subcommittee
  • Joint City Council/School Committee
  • Leadership, Accountability and Measurement Subcommittee
  • Parent and Community Engagement Committee
    • Motion: Ms. Lubold made a motion to acknowledge the purpose statement as amended, The Parent and Caregiver Engagement Ad Hoc Committee is charged with reviewing and strengthening the school’s committee partnership with the DPAC, Special Education Parent Advisory Council, and the English Learner Parent Advisory Council. The latter two as required by Massachusetts law. And with identifying additional ways the committee can support meaningful family engagement through policy and oversight. The committee will monitor progress in collaboration with DPAC, SEPAC, and ELPAC, gather input from families, district partners, and bring forward recommendations for policies, practices, accountability structures that elevate family voice in planning, program development, and district improvement efforts
    • Motion:  The Ad-Hoc committee’s work is ongoing rather than time-limited, reflecting the long-term nature of strengthening family engagement. The committee will operate on an initial one-year timeline, with a formal check-in and reassessment of progress at the six-month mark. Expected outcomes for this period include increased parent and caregiver involvement in DPAC, CPAC, and ELPAC, greater visibility of the school committee’s engagement efforts within the community, stronger two-way communication channels between families and the school committee. And regular reports from parent leaders of those committees to the full school committee, modeled on the structure of existing student representative reports. The school committee and parents in the district develop and encourage parent leaders to lead this important work with their committees.
    • Motion: The matter of definition of meaningful parent and caregiver engagement that the meaningful parent and caregiver engagement is ongoing… is an ongoing two-way relationship between families and the school committee and the district, characterized by accessible pathways for families to share feedback and experiences directly with the school committee and the district beyond public comment and periodic surveys. Clear communication to parents and caregivers about why their participation matters and how their input will be used, authentic dialogue that goes beyond one-time or transactional interactions, and formal recognition of families as essential partners in supporting student success and strengthening school committee decision-making.
